Visit note | 2025-02-19 12:30 PM | Dr. Farhana Kabir, General Medicine | Patient: Habiba Kabir, 59, female. Mrs. Kabir presents for her first visit reporting constant tiredness, feeling breathless when climbing stairs, and noticing that her nails have become quite brittle. She works as a fisherman and mentions that her symptoms worsened after a long spell of poor meals while living alone in Mohammadpur. She denies chest pain, palpitations, or gastrointestinal bleeding. On physical examination, her haemoglobin is 9.2 g/dL, blood pressure is 115/80 mmHg, pulse is 86 bpm, and weight is 72 kg. Conjunctivae appear pale. Assessment: Iron deficiency anaemia. Plan: a prescription was issued for iron supplementation. She was advised to eat more lentils, spinach, liver, and eggs, and to avoid tea within an hour of meals. Follow-up is scheduled in 6 weeks with a repeat haemoglobin test.

Visit note | 2025-02-19 12:30 PM | Dr. Selina Parvin, Neurology | Patient: Nurul Ahmed, 73, male. Mr. Ahmed returns for review, reporting dizziness when looking up, brief spinning sensations when turning over in bed, and accompanying nausea during these episodes. He works as a shopkeeper and notes that the trouble began after bumping his head on a rickshaw hood in Rajshahi. He has no focal neurological deficits or hearing loss. On examination, the Dix-Hallpike test is positive on the right side, with other vitals showing BP 116/80 mmHg, pulse 77 bpm, and weight 91 kg. Assessment: Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo. Plan: a prescription was issued to manage symptoms. Advice includes getting up slowly from bed, avoiding sudden head movements, and repeating the Epley manoeuvre at home as demonstrated. Follow-up in 2 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-02-19 04:00 PM | Dr. Towhid Alam, ENT | Patient: Shahidul Matubbar, 59, male. Mr. Matubbar attends for a follow-up visit regarding recurrent sneezing fits and itchy eyes that become much worse around dust. He works as a restaurant cook and states his discomfort has been worse since keeping a cat at home in Tangail. He reports no fever or shortness of breath. Examination reveals about 11 sneezing fits a day, with BP 114/78 mmHg, pulse 82 bpm, and weight 64 kg. Nasal mucosa is pale and boggy. Assessment: Allergic rhinitis. Plan: a prescription was issued to control allergic symptoms. He was advised to avoid dust, wear a mask when cleaning, and wash his bedding weekly. Follow-up is recommended in 1 month.

Visit note | 2025-02-20 02:00 PM | Dr. Sabrina Chowdhury, Cardiology | Patient: Ehsan Dewan, 64, male. Visit note | 2025-02-20 02:00 PM | Dr. Faisal Karim, Psychiatry | Patient: Habiba Chowdhury, 25, female. Ms. Chowdhury presents for her first visit with complaints of low energy and poor sleep. Follow-up is arranged in 1 month with her recorded home blood pressure readings.
